premise: What if you fell into a black hole? (a blocky astronaut takes the plunge; every step is real, sourced science)
title:
WHAT IF YOU
FELL INTO A
BLACK HOLE?

lines.text: What if you fell into a black hole?
Pick a small one. When a star around twenty times the Sun's mass dies, its core collapses into one.

facts.claim: NASA: a star of around 20 times the Sun's mass or more collapses into a stellar-mass black hole.
facts.quote: If it had around 20 times the Sun's mass or more, the star's core collapses into a stellar-mass black hole

lines.text: First you see a swirling disk of hot gas, glowing around it.

facts.claim: NASA: a black hole is surrounded by a swirling accretion disk of hot gas.
facts.quote: surrounded by a swirling accretion disk of hot gas

lines.text: Its gravity warps space time, so even light has to bend around it.

facts.claim: NASA: the black hole's gravitational field warps space-time and light must follow this distorted path.
facts.quote: warps space-time, the fabric of the universe, and light must follow this distorted path

lines.text: Get any closer and you are squeezed sideways and stretched long, like a noodle. Scientists call it spaghettification.

facts.claim: NASA: spaghettification; matter is squeezed horizontally and stretched vertically, resembling a noodle.
facts.quote: squeezed horizontally and stretched vertically, resembling a noodle

lines.text: Then the event horizon. Past this line, escaping would need more than the speed of light.

facts.claim: NASA: inside the event horizon the velocity needed to escape exceeds the speed of light.
facts.quote: the velocity needed to escape the black hole exceeds the speed of light

lines.text: Nothing goes faster than light. So whatever falls in stays in. Even light.

facts.claim: NASA: whatever passes into the event horizon is doomed to stay inside it, even light.
facts.quote: whatever passes into the event horizon is doomed to stay inside it

lines.text: And whatever happens to you next, nobody outside can ever find out.

facts.claim: NASA: nothing about what happens within them can reach an outside observer.
facts.quote: nothing about what happens within them can reach an outside observer

lines.text: Which makes it the perfect place for your search history.
